Title: Political action (for Sabbat?): Sacrifice for the leader

Messages.Author: Joscha
Messages.Body:
Sacrifice for the leader
Political action
(Requires an Archbishop, Priscus, Cardinal, Regent)
Worth 1 Vote
Choose a (sabbat) vampire in play. Succesful referendum gives that vampire blood up to his capacity.

This is a strong vote letting you bloat. It could be a way to make Sabbat vote stronger (in giving them a good way to bloat) and counter their disadvantage of not having Parity Shift and Reckless Agitation. It is better than Fifth Tradition, although you have to push through a referendum. The advantage over Voter Captivation is that you don't need vast majority in vote to fill up. The disadvantage is that nothing else happens for winning the referendum (no damage on other meth's pool or banishing a vampire for example).
Villein and this vote is a very good way of bloating for big'uns, only comparable to Renewed Vigor, an action only the scarce Salubri can do. So limiting it to Sabbat would be better. That could give them an edge in the comparision to Camarilla.
What do you think.

Baron of Frankfurt

Messages.Author: Surreal
Messages.Body: I am not so big fan of strong cards which creates blood from nothing with no heavy restrictions (like voter captivation). They lead to more timeouts and slower games. I would like to see that vote more like stronger version of Free States Rant which moves some blood from other vampires to your vampires.

Wow, wouldn't that be cool? But that even makes it stronger, isn't it? Because not only your minion gets blood, other minions are losing it.

That way?:
Sacrifice for the leader
Requires a Sabbat vampire.
Allocate X points among one or more ready vampires, where X is half the capacity of the acting vampire (rounded up). No more than 3 points can be allocated to each vampire (?). Successful referendum means each vampire moves 1 blood to the acting vampire for each point assigned.

That way the name of the card has to be changed, because the robbed vampires don't sacrifice their blood, it is stolen from them. Maybe "Blood for the leader" would be more fitting.

I like the idea of this card as long as it doesn't work too easily or cheaply. Another version might be...

Purity in the Ranks (there is already a card called sacrifice)
Political Action
Requires a Sabbat Vampire
Select another sabbat vampire. If this referendum is successful, that vampire gains blood to his or her capacity. Sabbat vampires get an additional vote during this referendum. If this referendum fails or is cancelled during the action, burn this acting vampire.

I've been tossing a very similar idea around in my head for a while, as an obvious alternative to Parity Shift.

In my head, it required a significant title (possibly including Seraph, which isn't actually a title), and perhaps used the same X = Methuselahs calculation as Parity Shift. A capacity-based option is probably okay, although it remains strong in the end game.

I wasn't happy with the ability to repeat this so much, though. Personally, I'd want a restriction that made it a strong play in small quantities, but possibly self-limiting. Once per turn still feels a bit easy. Maybe a "Put this card on this acting vampire. A vampire who has a Card Name on him cannot take the Card Name action." That doesn't feel quite right either.

I might also restrict it to taking blood from vampires who are younger than the acting vampire.

Messages.Author: jAvel

Move blood between your vampires is boring idea. I think this card should fulfill 3 criteria: a Leader, a Sacrifice and some usefullness.
For example, "leader" - gain blood / gain pool. "Sacrifice" - 1 agg damage to caller. "Usefullness" - minion damage / pool damage.

Sacrifice to the Leader
Political action. Require sabbat vampire.
Choose a titled sabbat vampire and assign up to 2 points between two other minions. Chosen titled sabbat vampire gains 3 blood, acting vampire takes 1 aggravated damage, and each minion with a point assigned either takes 3 unpreventable damage or his controller burns 2 pool.

- gain 3 blood
- torporize own minion
- deal 6 minion damage or 4 pool damage

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
There is a bug in your wording: you cannot do pool damage to a player with no minions. Better word it like Revolutionary council:

Sacrifice to the Leader
Political action. Require sabbat vampire.
Choose a titled sabbat vampire and allocate 2 points between two other minions and methuselahs. Successful referendum means that the chosen titled sabbat vampire gains 3 blood, the acting vampire takes 1 aggravated damage, each minion takes 3 unpreventable damage for each point assigned and each methuselah burns 2 pool for each point assigned.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Non-existant user wrote:
> There is a bug in your wording: you cannot do pool damage to a player with no minions.
>
That's not necessarily a bad thing. It's quite nice if powerful political actions have a built-in self-limiting mechanism. e.g. it's hard to chain multiple Parity Shift in one turn without passing your opponent's pool total.

A powerful political action that is good in the early game but trickier in the late game (when all the vampires are dead) would be a pretty neat thing to have, so it might require you allocate points to ready vampires, or ready minions.

On the flip-side, you can also have cards that are okay in the early game but great in the late game - Foreshadowing Destruction being a good example here. The DOM level is unplayable until you get people low-ish on pool, and then it can be great. A political action that was a bit 'meh' in the early game, and pretty strong in the late game, would be neat too.

> Ohlmann wrote:

Well, having a good vote (or other good action) will speed things along. A prey on 8 pool may take a couple of turns to eat through, giving your grand-prey unnecessary time to prepare, and so on.

That's why, from a design perspective, I quite like cards that force you to make interesting choices - do I play a lot of these, and maybe choke on them? do I discard this now? do I call it on my grand-prey, but that means my prey doesn't get ousted just yet?
